statusNote: Regent historically split top leadership between a 'President' (day-to-day CEO) and founder Pat Robertson's 'Chancellor' title (held continuously 1980-2023). Since Carlos Campo's 2013 resignation, the university has not named a separate President; the Chancellor (Pat Robertson, then Gordon Robertson) has functioned as chief executive, with a Provost handling academics. Timeline below reflects the effective top-executive chain, noting each person's actual title.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean/Founding Faculty, School of Communication and the Arts
leaders.nextRole: Distinguished Professor/Chair of Visual Communication; later C.S. Lewis Chair of Communication and Christian Thought
leaders.notes: Title held: President. Resigned the presidency in 1997 to return to teaching at Regent.

leaders.priorTitle: President, National Defense University (retired U.S. Army Lieutenant General)
leaders.nextRole: Private sector executive (Loral Corp., Lockheed Martin, and defense/logistics contracting)
leaders.notes: Title held: President. Retired U.S. Army lieutenant general and West Point graduate; died 2011.

leaders.priorTitle: Founder and Chancellor
leaders.notes: Title held: President (concurrently also Chancellor, a title he held continuously from 1980). Announced retirement as president effective July 1, 2010, succeeded by Carlos Campo.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior administrator overseeing accreditation (joined Regent staff in 2008)
leaders.notes: 8th president and first Latino president of a regionally accredited Christian university in the U.S. Resigned suddenly and without public explanation just weeks into the fall 2013 term (August-October 2013); became Ashland University's president in 2015.

leaders.priorTitle: Chancellor
leaders.notes: Per university bylaws, Robertson (already Chancellor) stepped in as CEO after Campo's abrupt resignation in 2013 and no new 'President' was subsequently named. He continued as Chancellor/CEO until his death on June 8, 2023.

leaders.priorTitle: President and CEO
leaders.notes: Named Chancellor in July 2023 succeeding his late father Pat Robertson; continues to concurrently serve as President/CEO of CBN and president of Operation Blessing.

leaders.priorTitle: Academic Vice President
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: Association of Jesuit Colleges and Universities (AJCU)
leaders.notes: 23rd president; joined Regis faculty in 1975, became academic VP in 1982, president in 1993; stepped down 2012 and led AJCU nationally starting 2013 (retired from AJCU 2019).

leaders.priorTitle: Associate Provost for Faculty Development
leaders.nextRole: No formal next role; remained affiliated with Regis leading the 'Manifest Magis' fundraising campaign
leaders.notes: 24th president, served 10 years; resigned effective December 31, 2021.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Franchise Relations (formerly Market CEO); Regis trustee and affiliate MBA professor
leaders.nextRole: Continued as Board of Trustees member
leaders.notes: First female and first lay leader of Regis University; served as interim president January 1, 2022 to December 9, 2022, working to reverse enrollment decline before handing off.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Mission
leaders.notes: Served as acting president for the final weeks of 2022 (December 9-31, 2022), bridging to Salvador Aceves' start on January 1, 2023; previously acting president of the Jesuit School of Theology in Berkeley.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer
leaders.notes: 27th (first lay and first Latino) permanent president, took office January 1, 2023; left to lead his alma mater, the University of San Francisco, starting August 1, 2025.

leaders.priorTitle: Associate Provost
leaders.notes: Named interim president effective July 21, 2025, succeeding Aceves; brings roughly 30 years of Jesuit higher-education leadership experience.
